statement_pin_required.convention: Fix finite G : SimpleGraph V, A B : Set V. An A–B path starts in A, ends in B, internals avoid A ∪ B. S separates A from B when every A–B path meets S. Claim: min |S| = max number of pairwise vertex-disjoint A–B paths. v1 is this global form (Diestel). Local κ(u,v) is the same heartbeat if cheap, not required. Encoding: Mathlib Walk / IsPath / Walk.support.
landmines: Finite only. Infinite / Erdős–Menger out of scope.
A ∩ B is load-bearing (trivial paths + every separator contains it).
Global form uses fully vertex-disjoint paths; local u–v form uses internally disjoint. v1 is global.
Not König ν=τ. Optional König engine on an auxiliary graph; do not re-prime konig-bipartite.
Not edge-Menger, not max-flow, not Tutte, not Whitney κ ≤ λ ≤ δ, not 4CT/5CT.
Walk-induction is the budget sink — name Diestel |E| induction or stop.
Do not re-prime greedy / Brooks A/B / Dilworth / Eulerian / Dirac / König.
statement_pin_required.canonical_source: K. Menger, Zur allgemeinen Kurventheorie, Fund. Math. 10 (1927) 96–115. Textbook: Diestel, Graph Theory, Menger's theorem (min vertices separating A from B = max disjoint A–B paths). Type pin: Mathlib Walk / IsPath / Walk.support. Edge-Menger and max-flow min-cut are different theorems, not this claim.

feasibility_shape: Level A: A ∩ B nonempty (trivial paths); singleton A,B joined by an edge; no A–B path ⇒ p = s = 0; easy p ≤ s; zero sorry. Level B: theorem menger_vertex by Diestel |E| induction (or König reduction). Cap two levels. No edge-Menger / no flows / no infinite.
